conventions.title: Trapezoidal rule
conventions.statement: AUC is integrated with the linear-up/log-down trapezoidal rule: linear on rising or flat segments, logarithmic on declining positive segments.

source.reference: Stated in the app/compute/nca.py module docstring; not independently re-verified against guidance in this slice.

conventions.title: AUC_last ends at Tlast
conventions.statement: AUC_last and AUMC_last end at Tlast, the last positive concentration. Zero or BLQ rows after it add no area, and AUC_inf extrapolates from Tlast once.

source.reference: PR #3 (drsyedzaidi/pharmagent#3); agrees with PKNCA 0.12.1 on the committed offline cross-check tables.

conventions.title: Measured zero
conventions.statement: An unflagged finite 0 is kept as an observed zero, but it is not a quantifiable concentration and never ends the leading-BLQ phase, in single-dose and steady-state data.

source.reference: Owner's rule recorded in PR #3 correction cycle (drsyedzaidi/pharmagent#3, commit d706954).

conventions.title: BLQ flag codes
conventions.statement: The BLQ flag accepts booleans, 1 or 0 as numbers or text, and Y/N, YES/NO or TRUE/FALSE in any case. A blank or missing cell, '.', NA or NaN is not flagged. Any other value stops the analysis with an error, so an unknown code never silently means not BLQ.

conventions.title: Pre-dose records
conventions.statement: Single-dose records before the dose time add no area before the dose. With no usable record at the dose time, the closest pre-dose record sets C = 0 there only when it is BLQ-flagged or a measured 0; a positive pre-dose value is never carried to the dose time.

conventions.title: Steady state: final-interval scope
conventions.statement: For steady-state data, the analysis uses the final dosing interval only, and rows with AMT above 0 build the dose schedule and are never concentrations. When a BLQ flag column is present, the BLQ leading/middle/trailing classification uses only the observation rows within that interval, so samples from earlier intervals play no part in it; the reported BLQ count covers all observation rows in the dataset.

conventions.title: Steady state: endpoint closure
conventions.statement: A complete steady-state profile spans exactly [0, tau]. At least one end must be measured. The start takes a sample from {snap_fraction} of tau before the dose to {pre_dose_tol} time units after it (a BLQ record there, normalised to a 0 baseline, counts); the tau end takes a sample within {snap_fraction} of tau of tau. The sample closest to each end is placed exactly at it. Every measured end uses a distinct closest sample; one sample never supplies both ends. At most one end may be supplied by the steady-state periodicity assumption (C(tau) = C(0) or C(0) = C(tau)), and that assumed closing segment must be integrable by linear-up/log-down. Each subject reports whether each end was measured or assumed, and the summary and rule text name the subjects with an assumed end.

source.reference: PR #3 (drsyedzaidi/pharmagent#3), commits d4b7be1 and d706954. No PKNCA steady-state reference exists.

alternatives: fail closed when the tau sample is BLQ (PharmAgent)
bridge to an assumed zero concentration
branch_point.changes_conclusion_when: bridging changes AUC_tau materially; one pinned case gave 18.13 against an analytic 11.20

known_gaps: The integration rule used for the assumed closing segment (log-down) is not reported as a separate result field; only the assumed end is reported.

conventions.title: Steady state: incomplete intervals
conventions.statement: A steady-state subject that cannot form a complete [0, tau] interval (neither end available, fewer than 3 usable samples, a conflicting duplicate, or an assumed closure that linear-up/log-down cannot integrate) stops the run with a per-subject reason. No subject is dropped silently, and repeated-dose data is never re-analysed as single-dose NCA.

conventions.title: Terminal window (lambda_z)
conventions.statement: Lambda_z is fitted over contiguous windows of at least {min_points} positive concentrations after Tmax that always end at the last point, and the window with the largest adjusted R-squared is chosen. A window needs a decline steeper than {min_lambda_z} per time unit (issue #12: this rejects floating-point noise on flat terminal phases) and a positive adjusted R-squared; otherwise no lambda_z is reported. Equal fits go to the longest window: a later, shorter window replaces the current best only when its adjusted R-squared is strictly greater than the stored best, rounded to 6 decimals.
known_gaps: PKNCA's default prefers more points on near-ties; lambda_z differed by under 0.6% on the committed cross-check tables. That difference is documented, not a tested convention.

alternatives: prefer more points within a tolerance of the best fit (PKNCA default)
branch_point.changes_conclusion_when: the window choice moves lambda_z enough to change AUC_inf, half-life or CL/F beyond the reviewer's tolerance

conventions.title: Average bioequivalence
conventions.statement: PharmAgent evaluates average bioequivalence only when the study design, regulatory profile, test formulation and reference formulation are explicitly supplied. Crossover analyses require valid subject, treatment and period identifiers, exactly two periods and at least two observed treatment sequences. Positive finite parameter values are analysed on the logarithmic scale. The selected regulatory profile controls the confidence level, acceptance limits and rounding policy. A crossover is analysed with a fixed-effects model with sequence, subject within sequence, period and formulation, and a parallel design as two independent groups. These estimators are interim until independent validation is complete and are not yet cleared as the regulatory model. Missing, excluded and invalid observations are reported in a parameter-level disposition ledger. Ambiguous, incomplete or unsupported designs fail closed rather than switching design or inferring the reference formulation.

source.reference: Owner decisions of 2026-10-23 on the BE safety contract (app/compute/be_contract.py). Profiles: FDA, Statistical Approaches to Establishing Bioequivalence (May 2026); ICH M13A, EMA/CHMP/ICH/953493/2022; EMA, CPMP/EWP/QWP/1401/98 Rev. 1/Corr**.

known_gaps: Half-up rounding of exact .xx5 ties is a PharmAgent implementation convention; the guidance does not define tie handling.
Independent validation of the 2x2 crossover model is pending: a cross-check against base R lm and nlme, and review by a biostatistician. Until then the outputs stay interim.

For complete two-period data the fixed-effects and mixed-model formulation estimates are expected to coincide because the subject effect cancels within subject; this is to be confirmed numerically against nlme and is not yet checked.
NTI (narrow therapeutic index), highly variable, replicate and reference-scaled designs are unsupported and are refused; so are multi-group data and crossovers with more than two periods.

A parallel design uses pooled variance by default; Welch is an explicit option. The guidance texts read do not choose between them (owner decision). Stratification factors and covariates for parallel designs (ICH M13A 2.2.3.4) are not supported.

conventions.title: Log-likelihood profiling cut-off
conventions.statement: Log-likelihood profiling limits are where the objective function worsens by the chi-square (1 df) quantile: {cutoff} at the {level_percent}% level. The objective function (OFV) is on the -2 log-likelihood scale, and the 3.84 value applies only on that scale with one degree of freedom.
known_gaps: The chi-square source is not yet cited. The scale is taken from app/compute/nlme.py (OFV = -2 log L); verify and cite a source before approval.
The -2 log-likelihood scale is stated from code documentation; no test pins it.

conventions.title: BLQ leading/middle/trailing rule
conventions.statement: With a BLQ flag, flagged records before a subject's first quantifiable value count as a 0 baseline (also when the value is blank); later flagged records, in the middle or trailing, are excluded from AUC and lambda_z. A record is quantifiable only when it is unflagged with a finite TIME and a finite positive DV.

source.reference: PR #3 (drsyedzaidi/pharmagent#3). The tool's result text calls this rule 'M1'; no authoritative source defining that name has been identified, so the catalog does not use it.

alternatives: keep middle BLQ as zero (PKNCA matched configuration)
branch_point.changes_conclusion_when: a flagged middle or trailing BLQ record changes AUC_last, AUC_inf or CL/F beyond the reviewer's tolerance
